title: Board and governing-body minutes review for audit-relevant events
problem: Minutes of boards, councils and committees are long and unstructured and must be read for debt, grants, related-party items, commitments and policy changes that change audit procedures.
approach: Staff upload a year of minutes; a saved template returns a dated summary of items an auditor would query.
The firm tunes the template prompt; a person reads each flagged item against the minutes and decides whether it changes procedures.
Harris, Hardy & Johnstone, a commercial-client firm, reports reviews taking about 5 minutes instead of about 1 hour (vendor-published).
A nonprofit-focused firm owner says a minutes review surfaced debt a client had not mentioned (one anecdote).
who: Harris, Hardy & Johnstone; a nonprofit-focused firm

title: Key-term extraction from bond indentures, grant agreements and other long agreements
problem: Debt agreements, grant awards and amendments are long, and auditors need restrictions, reporting requirements, deadlines and covenants to design procedures.
approach: The auditor uploads the agreement and a template extracts terms into a report.
For grants, the vendor says the tool identifies restrictions, reporting requirements and deadline obligations to help design procedures.
A firm owner says a 750-page bond indenture produced a report in three to four minutes (vendor-published); no manual comparison is given.
The auditor agrees extracted terms to the source before relying on them.

title: Donor agreement and conditional-grant classification support
problem: Donor letters are often vague, and classifying gifts as restricted, conditional or endowment-related drives net asset presentation and later releases from restriction.
approach: A prompt asks the assistant to read donor correspondence and agreements and propose a classification with rationale and open questions for management.
A vendor says three nonprofit-focused firms use its tool for donor restriction tracking (vendor-published); no measure is given.
Accounting and legal judgment decides the classification; the auditor tests management's conclusion.

title: First-draft inherent risk assessment by assertion for newer staff
problem: Assessing inherent risk of material misstatement by assertion is a concept juniors need a senior to walk through, and the knowledge sits with few people in small firms.
approach: Staff enter client facts and ask the assistant for an inherent risk assessment by assertion, which they must read, test and own.
The owner uses it as scaffolding so staff can start without a senior.
The Forde Firm owner says staff can now engage with inherent risk at assertion level without her walking them through it (vendor-published).
A manager reviews the risk assessment and a partner approves.

title: Citation-backed technical research on nonprofit, government and grant-compliance questions
problem: Small governmental and nonprofit audit teams answer technical questions by calling another CPA or specialist or searching several libraries, which is slow and depends on who is available.
approach: Staff ask an AI research assistant grounded in accounting and audit literature and the firm's templates, and get cited answers.
The vendor says users can check Uniform Guidance and questioned costs without calling a government audit specialist.
In Plante Moran's pilot, 91% of respondents said it was faster than traditional research and 62% reported significant time savings (vendor-published).
Staff verify citations and apply the guidance to the client's facts; a reviewer signs off.
who: Plante Moran; a small firm owner

title: Population analysis, risk-based sampling and linked documentation at small nonprofit audit firms
problem: Small firms pick samples by hand across disconnected spreadsheets and tools, then write the documentation peer reviewers expect; both steps take hours and vary by staff member.
approach: An audit analytics module loads the population, splits it into risk groups, selects a statistically supported sample and writes linked documentation.
The pattern is segmentation and sample selection, not whole-population testing; the auditor sets the strata and approves the sample.
The Forde Firm's owner says hand-picking a sample takes about three hours and the software does it in about five minutes (vendor-published).
Three firm owners say the documentation eased peer review (vendor-published); a reviewer still inspects it because peer reviewers read it as evidence.

title: Excel agents for grant compliance tests and payroll sampling in government audits
problem: Regional firms with many similar government clients, such as about 70 school districts, receive data as large, inconsistently formatted PDFs, and single-audit compliance tests are long.
approach: A DataSnipper Excel agent extracts from differently formatted documents, selects payroll samples and runs compliance tests, each tied to a source snip.
Pattillo Brown & Hill ran a grant compliance test on 63 items in about an hour and is building trial-balance agents (vendor-published).
Perry & Associates, using OCR rather than an agent, reports one 50-fund client's workpaper preparation fell from 80 to 25 hours (vendor-published).
A reviewer clicks a cell and sees the supporting document; results are traced and locked in.
who: Pattillo Brown & Hill, Perry & Associates, DataSnipper

title: Idea: check the draft federal awards schedule against award documents and ledger
problem: Idea, not a deployment: the schedule of expenditures of federal awards must match award notices, ledger, pass-through amounts, clusters and period of performance, and errors surface during the audit.
approach: Idea: a prompt asks the assistant to compare the draft schedule with grant agreements, prior-year schedules and ledger detail.
It would list missing programs, wrong Assistance Listing numbers, spending outside the performance period and possible duplicates, separating confirmed errors from questions.
Management owns the schedule; the auditor tests it independently.

title: Footnote-to-statement tie-out of nonprofit and government financial statements
problem: Auditors manually agree footnote numbers to the face statements and schedules, and copy-and-paste steps cause small differences that surface late.
approach: A saved reconciliation template reads the statements and notes and lists every number that does not agree, down to a dollar.
The firm says it catches differences including a one-dollar difference and reduces copy-and-paste mistakes (vendor-published; no count of differences found).
The preparer clears each listed difference.

title: Disclosure checklist review agent in the audit file; nonprofit sets not described
problem: Disclosure checklists for nonprofit and governmental statements are long and checked by hand late in the audit.
approach: An agent in the audit platform reviews the financial statements and returns citation-backed suggestions.
The auditor accepts, edits or overrides each suggestion in the engagement.
Caseware says the agent saves 2.7 review hours per workflow on average (vendor-published); basis, sample and engagement types are not stated.
It is a general audit product; nonprofit and government disclosure sets are not described.

title: Idea: management-side audit readiness with AI prompts for finance teams
problem: Idea, not a deployment: small nonprofit finance teams answer long audit request lists under time pressure; 60% of nonprofits in one vendor survey rely on one full-time person.
approach: Idea: a national firm's playbook gives finance teams prompts to sort audit request lists by owner and source and draft fluctuation explanations.
The prompts also check schedules for footing errors and draft estimate memos, in approved tools only; the playbook says outputs are drafts.
The finance director validates every explanation against actual activity before it goes to auditors.

title: Screening grant documents for policy-restricted language before submission (university research office)
problem: Grant writers must remove language that new federal or state policy restricts, and manual review is slow and delays submissions.
approach: A university research office tool combines rule-based matching with a private-cloud language model to flag sensitive terms and suggest alternatives.
On five annotated grant documents it flagged 16 of 22 policy-sensitive terms with no false positives (precision 1.00, recall 0.73) (self-reported).
Its F1 of 0.84 beat GPT-4o (0.43) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (0.72, not significantly); usability scored 85.9 from 25 testers (self-reported).
The author accepts or rejects each suggestion.

title: Federal agency AI analysis of single audit history to target noncompliance (HHS)
problem: Federal agencies must ensure audits are submitted on time and findings corrected, and HHS says repeat findings and delinquent audits went unaddressed for years.
approach: HHS's finance office says it is analysing single audit information across all 50 states with AI tools covering at least five years.
It has written to governors and treasurers, lists remedies including withholding payments and disallowing costs, and is examining audit rigor.
HHS reports hundreds of grantees have not submitted required audits, some by over two years (self-reported); no AI performance measure is given.
HHS staff send letters and decide on remedies; the press release does not describe review of AI outputs.

title: State audit offices use AI on large spending datasets with human verification
problem: State and local government audits involve large transaction sets, such as purchasing-card spending, and small audit teams.
approach: The North Carolina State Auditor says the office uses industry partners to apply AI to large datasets, then verifies findings with people.
Washington's State Auditor publishes a governed-use AI policy with a staff review requirement and oversight committee, but describes no audit uses.
North Carolina's auditor says AI helps find a needle in a haystack and made purchasing-card audits more efficient (self-reported); no counts.
People verify what the AI finds before results are accepted.
who: NC State Auditor, Washington State Auditor

title: AI error check and chatbot inside Form 990 e-file software
problem: Form 990-series filings need schedules, support and consistency checks, and errors cause rejections and penalties.
approach: The e-file product runs an AI-powered check for potential issues before submission and offers a chatbot for filing questions.
The vendor says it is working on improvements to AI validation.
Feature description only (vendor-published); no error rates are published.
The preparer reviews and signs; the check is not an approval.

title: IRS tool to screen and prioritise public referrals about exempt organizations
problem: The IRS exempt organization examination unit receives public referrals and runs data-driven compliance exams based on Form 990 data.
approach: An IRS letter, summarised by EY, says an AI tool to screen and prioritise public referrals was planned for fiscal 2024.
Data-driven exams based on Form 990 information found employment taxes, unrelated business income and underreported compensation as the most prominent issues.
About 76% of closed exempt-organization exams in fiscal 2023 led to a tax change (self-reported); not a measure of the AI tool.
A human checkpoint is not described.
